text:
The question is about the South Pole, and the usual "discovered" year is 1911, when Roald Amundsen's expedition reached it on 14 December 1911.

1911

Shelley's sonnet "Ozymandias" was written in December 1817 and published in The Examiner on 11 January 1818.

1817

Jude the Apostle's birth year is not recorded in any source, so any answer is an estimate. He was a contemporary of Jesus, and Jesus is usually placed at about 4 BCE to 6 BCE. Jude is traditionally said to have been martyred around 65 to 70 CE (some accounts say 65 CE in Beirut). A birth year near 1 BCE fits that tradition and the contemporary timeline, though it is only a guess.

-1

Himeji Castle's history: first fortification in 1333 by Akamatsu Norimura (Himeyama fort), the castle rebuilt in 1346 by Akamatsu Sadanori; Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1580 constructed a three-story keep; Ikeda Terumasa's major expansion was 1601-1609, creating the current form. Wikidata "inception" is often 1333 for Himeji Castle. The Wikipedia infobox says "Built 1333, rebuilt 1609." I'll go with 1333.

1333

The Alexander Mosaic is from the House of the Faun in Pompeii, dated to around 100 BCE (late 2nd century BCE). It is a copy of a Hellenistic painting, probably from around 310 BCE. The mosaic itself is usually dated to about 120-100 BCE, and I'll go with -100.

-100

Porter is traditionally said to have originated in London in the early 18th century. The name is commonly linked to Ralph Harwood's "Entire" in 1722, though that account is disputed. Wikipedia says porter was developed in London in the early 1700s, and the style is often dated to 1722.

1722

The Liberty Bell was cast in 1752 by the Whitechapel Foundry in London. It cracked on arrival, and was recast by Pass and Stow in Philadelphia in 1753. The usual "created" date is 1752.

1752

The Old Kingdom is conventionally dated from the Third Dynasty, beginning around 2686 BCE (some sources give 2700 BCE or 2686 BCE).

-2686

The Nok culture of central Nigeria is generally dated from about 1500 BCE to about 1 CE, so the end date is 1 CE (some sources give 300 CE). Wikipedia says "Nok culture... appeared around 1500 BCE and vanished under unknown circumstances around 1 CE" and I'm using that figure.

1

Amer Fort in Jaipur was begun by Raja Man Singh I in 1592. Earlier structures on the site date to the 11th–12th century, but the fort as it stands is generally dated to 1592.

1592

Batu Caves temple was founded in 1890 by K. Thamboosamy Pillai, who installed the Murugan statue and temple; the Sri Subramaniar Swamy temple was dedicated in 1891 (the Thaipusam festival began in 1892). The commonly cited founding year is 1891.

1891

York Minster's origins: the first church was a wooden structure built in 627 for the baptism of King Edwin of Northumbria. The current Gothic building was begun around 1220 and completed in 1472. The question asks for "year created / founded", and 627 is the most likely answer for the founding.

627

Barabbas appears in the Gospels as the prisoner released instead of Jesus around 30-33 CE. The Bible gives no account of his death, and later traditions about it are unreliable. Since the card needs a single year, I'll go with a date tied to his only known moment in history, the trial of Jesus, which is most often placed at 33 CE (30 CE is the other common choice).

33

The Four Seasons were formed in 1960 under that name (the group's earlier incarnations date to 1956, as the Variatones, and later the Four Lovers). Wikipedia lists the group as active from 1960.

1960

The Nanjing Massacre began on December 13, 1937, and lasted about six weeks, ending in early to mid-January 1938. The year it ended is 1938.

1938

Estimating Japheth's birth year requires a chronology, and the usual choice is Ussher's. Ussher puts the Flood at 2348 BCE. Noah was 500 when he begat Shem, Ham and Japheth, and 600 at the Flood. Ussher dates Japheth's birth to 2446 BCE, with Shem born two years after the Flood begins... Specifically, Shem was 100 two years after the Flood, so Shem was born in 2448 BCE. Japheth is usually listed as the eldest, though the Hebrew is ambiguous. Ussher's own chronology gives Noah's sons as born around 2448 BCE, with Japheth often placed at 2448 BCE.

Ussher placed Noah's sons' births at about 2448 BCE, which would make Japheth's year -2448.

-2448

The Academy Awards were first presented in 1929, honoring films from 1927/28. The Best Actress award was created with the first ceremony, so the year is 1929 (the awards were established in 1927 and Janet Gaynor won the first one).

The question asks for the year created/founded, and the first ceremony was in 1929, so I'll go with that.

1929

Jean Lafitte's birth year is uncertain; sources give anywhere from about 1776 to 1782. The most commonly cited year is 1780.

1780

Umar ibn al-Khattab was born around 584 CE, though some sources give about 583 or 586. The commonly cited year is 584.

584

Sweyn Forkbeard's birth year is uncertain. Sources usually give c. 963 or 960, and some give 962 or 965. I'm going with 963.

963

Devanagari evolved from Brahmi via Gupta and Nagari scripts, with the Nagari form attested from roughly the 1st-7th centuries CE. It is often dated to around the 7th century CE, with its standardized form emerging by about 1000 CE. Wikipedia's infobox gives "1st to 4th century CE" for its development, and for the Nagari form "7th century CE". I'll go with 700.

700

The question asks for the earliest year associated with cattle, which I read as when they were first domesticated. Archaeological evidence puts domestication of cattle (Bos taurus) at roughly 8000 BCE in the Near East, so I take -8000 as the best single year.

-8000

The Jacobean era corresponds to the reign of James I of England, who died in 1625. It is usually dated from his accession to the English throne in 1603 to his death in 1625.

1625

The question asks for a single year for the founding of the Russian Orthodox Church. Several dates are plausible:

- 988: the Christianization of Kievan Rus' under Vladimir.
- 1448: de facto autocephaly, when Jonah was elected without Constantinople's approval.
- 1589: the establishment of the Moscow Patriarchate, with Job as the first patriarch.

Wikipedia's infobox gives the founding as 988 ("Baptism of Rus'"), and its autocephaly entry gives 1448 as the date of de facto autocephaly. Since the question stresses "autocephalous" and "created", 1448 or 1589 could be intended, but the most common answer for "founded" is 988.

988

LINE was launched in Japan in June 2011 by NHN Japan (a subsidiary of Naver) after the March 2011 Tōhoku earthquake.

2011

Rouen Cathedral's construction as the current Gothic building began in 1202 after a fire, though the earlier Romanesque cathedral was consecrated in 1063. The Wikidata "inception" is probably 1030 or 1200. The cathedral's own history dates the Gothic building to 1202, and the "year created" is most plausibly 1202.

1202

The House of Grimaldi is traditionally dated to Otto Canella's consul status in Genoa, but the dynasty's name comes from his son Grimaldo, in the 12th century. The Grimaldi seized the Rock of Monaco in 1297 under François Grimaldi. The "founded" date in Wikipedia's infobox for the House of Grimaldi is 1160, which is the year commonly given for the founding of the house.

1160

Traditional chronology (Nihon Shoki) gives Jimmu's birth as 711 BCE (he is said to have ascended the throne in 660 BCE at age 52). Traditional dating: born 711 BCE.

-711

The question asks for a founding year for the Catholic Church in the United States. The most common answer is 1789, when John Carroll was appointed the first bishop (Diocese of Baltimore, created in 1789). The Wikipedia infobox for the Catholic Church in the United States doesn't give a clear founding year, but a trivia card would likely use 1789.

1789

The House of Plantagenet as a royal dynasty began with Henry II's accession in 1154. The Angevin line itself traces to Geoffrey Plantagenet, Count of Anjou, but the "year created" for the royal dynasty is most commonly given as 1154.

1154

The Latter Day Saint movement is usually dated to 1830, when Joseph Smith organized the Church of Christ on April 6 of that year. Some accounts instead point to the First Vision in 1820 or to the publication of the Book of Mormon in 1830, but the 1830 organization is the standard founding date.

1830

The Bengal Sultanate is conventionally dated from 1352, when Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah unified Bengal's regions. Some sources instead give 1342, the year Ilyas Shah took power in Lakhnauti. Wikipedia lists the Bengal Sultanate as founded in 1352, though the independent sultanate is often traced to 1338, when Fakhruddin Mubarak Shah established independence in Sonargaon. The 1352 date is the most common for the unified sultanate.

1352

The Dukedom of Cornwall was created in 1337 by Edward III for his son Edward, the Black Prince. It was the first English dukedom.

1337

The earliest Tamil records are the Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions, usually dated to around the 3rd century BCE. Some scholars date the Adichanallur and Keezhadi finds earlier, but the most commonly cited earliest records are the cave inscriptions from roughly 300 BCE. Wikipedia says Tamil's earliest inscriptions date to about 600 BCE, though it also says the earliest period of Tamil literature dates to about 300 BCE. For a trivia card, -300 is the safest answer.

-300

Diprotodon, the largest known marsupial, is generally dated to have gone extinct around 44,000 years ago, though some estimates place it nearer 25,000 years ago. Using the commonly cited figure of about 44,000 years ago, I convert to a year: 44,000 years before present is roughly 42,000 BCE, since "present" is taken as 1950 CE. That gives -42000.

-42000

The Fourth Crusade ran from 1202 to 1204, ending with the sack of Constantinople in April 1204.

1204

The Duchy of Lancaster was created in 1351 for Henry of Grosmont (first Duke). The title "Duke of Lancaster" held by the reigning monarch dates from 1399, when Henry IV became king and the duchy merged with the crown. But the question asks "year created / founded", most likely 1351.

1351

Clovis I is generally said to have been born around 466 CE. The exact year is uncertain, and some sources give 466 while others say c. 467.

466

The question asks for the year the mammoth genus ended. Woolly mammoths on Wrangel Island survived until about 4,000 years ago (roughly 2000 BCE), and the last known population died out around 1650 BCE according to some sources. Dating cards often use approximately -2000 for this.

Estimates for the Wrangel Island extinction range from about 4,000 to 3,700 years ago. The commonly cited figure is around 2000 BCE.

-2000

Arnhem received city rights in 1233 from Count Otto II of Guelders. The question asks for the year the municipality was created or founded, and the usual Wikidata-style answer is the city rights year of 1233.

1233

Farrukhsiyar was born on 20 August 1685.

1685

Methuselah is a biblical figure, so any birth year depends on which chronology is used. Ussher's chronology puts Methuselah's birth at 3317 BCE (Anno Mundi 687). The Masoretic text gives him birth in AM 687, and Ussher dates Creation to 4004 BCE, so 4004 − 687 = 3317 BCE.

-3317

Okinawa Prefecture was established in 1879 when Japan annexed the Ryukyu Kingdom (Ryukyu Disposition). Earlier, in 1872, the Ryukyu Domain was created, but the prefecture itself dates to 1879.

1879

The question asks for the earliest year associated with universal basic income. The idea is usually traced to Thomas More's Utopia (1516), which discusses guaranteed income to deter theft. Juan Luis Vives proposed a minimum income for the poor in 1526, and Thomas Paine's Agrarian Justice followed in 1797. The earliest of these, and the one most often cited, is Utopia.

1516

The Phoenician alphabet is usually given as c. 1050 BCE to c. 150 BCE (some sources say 150 CE for Punic and Neo-Punic use). The question asks for the year it ended, and trivia cards of this kind (such as the Wikipedia infobox for the Phoenician alphabet) list the time period as "c. 1050 BCE – 150 BCE". That points to -150.

-150

The Maccabees as a group emerged with the Maccabean Revolt, which began in 167 BCE when Mattathias started the rebellion.

-167

Reims Cathedral's construction began in 1211 after a fire destroyed the earlier church in 1210. The "year created/founded" is most commonly given as 1211.

1211

Octavia the Younger was born around 69 BCE. Her father Gaius Octavius died in 59 BCE. Her birth year is commonly given as c. 69 BCE, and some sources say 64 BCE, but 69 is the most common.

-69

Ramune was first created in Japan in 1884 by Alexander Cameron Sim, a Scottish pharmacist in Kobe, who sold a lemonade-style drink called "Ramune". The drink is often dated to 1884, when it was first sold in Japan.

1884

Queen Anne's War ended with the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713. The treaty was signed in April 1713, and in North America the war is generally dated 1702–1713.

1713

Caesar crossed the Rubicon in January 49 BCE, and the phrase "Alea iacta est" is attributed to that moment.

-49

Clipperton Island was discovered by Europeans on Good Friday, April 3, 1711, by French captains Michel Du Bocage and Martin de Chassiron. Some accounts date a Spanish sighting to 1528 (Álvaro de Saavedra), but the standard answer for its discovery is 1711, and the island is named for the pirate John Clipperton, who visited later.

1711

Ishmael is traditionally placed as Abraham's son, born when Abraham was 86. Abraham's birth is traditionally dated around 1996 BCE by Jewish chronology (Anno Mundi 1948), which puts Ishmael's birth around 1910 BCE. Other estimates differ: some date Abraham to about 2000 BCE, which gives Ishmael's birth around 1910 BCE as well, so I'll use that.

-1910

Neoplatonism is conventionally said to end in 529 CE, when Justinian closed the Platonic Academy in Athens. Some date the end of the school later, since Neoplatonic teaching continued in Alexandria, but the Academy's closure is the common marker.

529

Caesar's Commentarii de Bello Gallico is generally dated to about 50 or 51 BCE. Most scholars think the first seven books were written in the winter of 52/51 BCE and published around 51 BCE, and Hirtius added an eighth book after Caesar's death. Both -51 and -50 are defensible, and I'm going with -51.

-51

Bucephalus was reportedly about 12 or 13 when Alexander tamed him, which is usually dated to around 344 or 343 BCE. That puts his birth around 355 or 356 BCE. Alexander himself was born in 356 BCE, and tradition often has the horse born at about the same time.

-355

The Indo-Scythians (Sakas in India) are usually dated from the Maues/Maues-era invasion of the Indian subcontinent. Wikipedia's infobox lists "Indo-Scythians" with a start around 200 BCE, but the kingdom of Maues is dated to about 110 BCE. The Wikipedia infobox for "Indo-Scythians" gives "c. 200 BCE – c. 400 CE", so I'll go with 200 BCE.

-200

Longinus is the traditional name of the centurion who pierced Christ's side at the crucifixion. He is a legendary figure, so no birth year is attested. Tradition places him in the 1st century, and a birth around 1 BCE to 10 CE is a plausible guess. Some trivia databases, such as Wikidata, might list him differently. I'll go with a rough estimate near the start of the era.

1

The Bronze Age ended at different times in different regions, so any single year is a convention. The Wikidata-style entry for "Bronze Age" gives an end time of about 600 BCE in some listings and about 1200 BCE in others. The usual Eurasian convention, with the Iron Age beginning around 1200 BCE (the Late Bronze Age collapse), points to -1200. Wikipedia's infobox for the Bronze Age lists roughly 3300–1200 BCE, so I'm going with that.

-1200

The Jacobin Club originated as the Breton Club in 1789 (Versailles, May-June 1789), later becoming the Society of Friends of the Constitution, known as Jacobins after moving to the Jacobin convent in Paris in October 1789. The commonly cited founding year is 1789.

1789

Showtime launched on July 1, 1976, as a premium cable channel, initially distributed by Viacom. It began as a regional service in 1976 and went national in 1978.

1976

Ancient Macedonia's founding is traditionally attributed to the Argead dynasty under Caranus or Perdiccas I, around 700 BCE. Wikipedia-style listings often give about 808 BCE for Caranus, and many trivia cards use roughly 700 BCE for the kingdom's founding. I'll go with -700.

-700

Capernaum was likely founded during the Hasmonean period, around the 2nd century BCE. Archaeological evidence suggests settlement from the Hellenistic period, with the village growing in the 2nd to 1st century BCE. A commonly cited founding date is about 150 BCE.

-150

Schönbrunn Palace's origins: Emperor Matthias reputedly discovered the "schöner Brunnen" in 1612. The Katterburg estate was acquired by the Habsburgs in 1569. The Baroque palace was commissioned by Leopold I, with Fischer von Erlach's design starting in 1696. Maria Theresa's remodeling began in 1743. Wikipedia says "Construction began in 1696." Hmm, which year to choose? The typical "built" date is 1696.

1696

The European Court of Human Rights was established in 1959, after the European Convention on Human Rights, which was signed in 1950 and entered into force in 1953. Some sources instead cite 1959 as the founding year because that is when the Court itself was set up and held its first election of judges.

1959

Ibrahim I, Ottoman sultan, was born 5 November 1615.

1615

The Kingdom of Italy within the Holy Roman Empire is usually dated to 962, when Otto I was crowned emperor. Otto had already taken the Lombard crown in 951, and the kingdom itself descends from the Carolingian Kingdom of Italy, which began in 774 with Charlemagne's conquest of the Lombards. Wikidata gives an inception date of 962 for this entity, so I am going with that.

962

The Babylonian captivity ended when Cyrus the Great of Persia issued his decree allowing the Jews to return, which is traditionally dated to 538 BCE.

-538

Saul's dates are traditionally estimated: reign around 1047–1010 BCE (Wikipedia-style dating). Born about 1080 BCE would be a reasonable estimate. Some sources give his birth as c. 1080 BCE, and I'll go with that.

-1080

The Sanhedrin is traditionally considered to have ended around 425 CE, when Theodosius II abolished the Patriarchate after the death of Gamaliel VI.

425

The Avignon Papacy ended in 1377, when Gregory XI returned the papal seat to Rome. The Western Schism began in 1378, and an Avignon line of antipopes continued afterward. The standard answer for the end of the period is 1377.

1377

Salome, daughter of Herodias and Herod II (Herod Boethus), is generally estimated to have been born around 14 CE. Josephus mentions her marriage to Philip the Tetrarch, who died in 34 CE. Her birth is commonly given as c. 10 CE, though the estimates vary. Wikipedia gives her birth as around 14 CE, so I'll go with that.

14

The Plague of Justinian began in 541 and is generally said to have lasted until 549 in Constantinople, though the first pandemic overall continued in recurring waves until about 750. The question asks for the year it ended, and the phrase "later northern Europe" suggests the whole pandemic, which ended around 750. Wikipedia's infobox for the Plague of Justinian gives "541–549", with the wider first pandemic running to 767 or 750. The card's description, "Pandemic that afflicted the Byzantine Empire, and later northern Europe", resembles the Wikipedia list of epidemics, which lists the Plague of Justinian as 541–542 with a death toll of 25–100 million. Going by that description, the end year would be 542.

I'm choosing between 542, 549, and 750. The list-of-epidemics entry is the closest match to the card's wording, so I'll go with 542.

542

Galileo first observed Saturn's rings in 1610 but did not recognize them as rings. Huygens identified them as a ring in 1655 (observed 1655, published 1656). "Discovered" is ambiguous, but the usual answer for the rings is 1610 (Galileo), while Huygens's identification came in 1655.

Wikipedia's "Rings of Saturn" says: "The rings were first observed by Galileo Galilei in 1610 with his telescope, but... Christiaan Huygens in 1655 was the first to describe them as a disk surrounding the planet." The typical trivia card lists the discovery as 1610.

1610

Æthelberht of Wessex was a son of Æthelwulf, and he reigned from 860 to 865. His exact birth year isn't recorded. He was younger than Æthelbald, who was born around 834, and older than Æthelred, who was born around 847. Estimates for Æthelberht's birth usually fall around 836 to 840, and 839 is a common guess.

The question needs a single year, so I'll go with the common estimate.

839

The question is vague: the Ottoman Empire was founded around 1299, and its flags changed over time. The red flag with a white crescent and star was formally adopted in 1844, while the empire's founding date is the more likely intent of "year created / founded".

The trivia card is likely based on a Wikipedia article titled "Flags of the Ottoman Empire", which would give the founding of the empire rather than a specific flag date. I'll go with the founding date.

1299

Publius Quinctilius Varus died in 9 CE at the Teutoburg Forest. His birth year is not firmly attested, but it is commonly given as 46 BCE. Some sources give about 47 BCE.

-46

The Frankfurt Stock Exchange is traditionally dated to 1585, when Frankfurt merchants established a regular exchange for currency rates. The Wikipedia entry gives its founding as 1585 (some sources cite 1590s). I'm going with 1585.

1585

The Führerbunker was built in two phases: the Vorbunker in 1936 and the main Führerbunker in 1944. The "year created" for the main bunker is most commonly given as 1944, completed that year.

1944

The Umayyad conquest of Hispania began in 711 with the landing of Tariq ibn Ziyad. The conquest of the Visigothic kingdom was largely complete by about 718 to 721. Wikipedia's infobox for the "Umayyad conquest of Hispania" gives the dates as 711–718. The conquest of Septimania ended around 720–721, so 718 is the best answer for the end of the main conquest.

718

The question asks for a founding year for the Maya civilization. Early Maya settlements date to around 2000 BCE (the Preclassic or Formative period), and Wikidata-style "inception" values often give approximately -2000.

-2000

Puss in Boots was first published by Charles Perrault in 1697 in "Histoires ou contes du temps passé". Earlier literary versions exist, such as Straparola's from 1553, but the best-known version is Perrault's.

1697

The question is ambiguous, but the most natural reading is when the institution of the Pharaoh ended. That is usually taken as the death of Cleopatra VII in 30 BCE, when Egypt became a Roman province.

-30

The Chola dynasty's founding date is uncertain. The earliest references to the Cholas appear in Ashokan edicts from around 273–232 BCE, and Wikipedia describes them as ancient. The question asks for a "year created/founded", which is likely drawn from a database such as Wikidata that gives an inception date. For the Chola dynasty, the inception is commonly listed as 300 BCE, though I am not certain of that figure. The Medieval Chola Empire began in 848 CE, but this card concerns the dynasty as one of the Three Crowned Kings, which points to the earlier, ancient period. I'll answer with -300.

-300

"Jack and the Beanstalk" was first published in 1734 as "The Story of Jack Spriggins and the Enchanted Bean" in Round About Our Coal-Fire. The better-known version was Benjamin Tabart's, published in 1807 as "The History of Jack and the Bean-Stalk". The question asks about the year published, and the earliest known print is 1734, but Tabart's 1807 edition is usually cited as the first well-known one. Wikipedia says: "The earliest known printed version is Benjamin Tabart's 1807 'The History of Jack and the Bean-Stalk'", and the 1734 Jack Spriggins version is described as an earlier related tale. I'll go with 1807.

1807

The Age of Reason was published in parts: Part I in 1794, Part II in 1795, and Part III in 1807. The first part is the best-known and the usual answer for the publication year.

1794

Ibrahim ibn Muhammad was born to Maria al-Qibtiyya in Dhu al-Hijjah 8 AH, which corresponds to roughly March-April 630 CE. He died in 10 AH (632 CE) at about 16-18 months old.

Dhu al-Hijjah 8 AH began around April 630 CE. The conquest of Mecca took place in January 630 (Ramadan 8 AH), so the birth followed it, in 630.

630

The Bent Pyramid at Dahshur was built under Pharaoh Sneferu, who reigned around 2600 BCE (roughly 2613–2589 BCE). Construction of the Bent Pyramid is generally dated to about 2600 BCE.

-2600

Mycenaean civilization is conventionally dated as ending around 1100 BCE, with the Bronze Age collapse and the palaces destroyed around 1200 BCE. Wikipedia's infobox for "Mycenaean Greece" gives c. 1750 – c. 1050 BCE. So the end year is -1050.

-1050

The Group of Seven grew out of the Group of Six, which first met in 1975, and Canada joined in 1976 to make it seven. Many sources date the founding to 1975, though the G7 name only applies from 1976. The finance ministers' "Group of Five" dates to 1973, but the G7 itself is usually dated to 1975.

1975

The Kingdom of Georgia is conventionally dated to the unification under Bagrat III in 1008. Some sources give 1008, others 1000 or 1010. The most common answer is 1008.

1008

Hero of Alexandria is generally thought to have been active around 62 CE, based on his description of a lunar eclipse that occurred in 62 CE. His birth year is not actually known, though many sources give c. 10 CE. I'll go with that conventional date.

10

Toledo's earliest record is in Livy, who describes Toletum as a small fortified city in 192 BCE, when the Romans under Marcus Fulvius Nobilior captured it.

-192

Murad I was born around 1326, though sources vary (1319 to 1326). The commonly cited year is 1326.

1326

Lü Bu's birth year is not recorded precisely. He died in 198 CE, and his birth year is often given as unknown, though some sources estimate around 160 CE. I'll go with that estimate.

160

The earliest firm evidence for Srivijaya is the Kedukan Bukit inscription, dated 683 CE. It records a founding-like expedition by Dapunta Hyang. Chinese records also mention the kingdom in the 670s, when the monk Yijing visited. Most trivia sources give the founding as 683.

683

William Kidd was born around 1654 in Dundee, Scotland (some sources say 1645). The commonly cited year is 1654.

1654

Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj died in 875 CE (261 AH). He compiled Sahih Muslim over about 15 years, and the work is generally dated to the mid-9th century. A common date given for its completion is around 261 AH, which corresponds to 875 CE. I'll go with the approximate completion date of 875.

875

The Canadian Armed Forces were created on 1 February 1968, when the Royal Canadian Navy, the Canadian Army, and the Royal Canadian Air Force were unified under the Canadian Forces Reorganization Act.

1968

Magadha as a kingdom is often dated to around 600 BCE, when it emerged as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas. Some sources date the Haryanka dynasty's rise to 544 BCE, and others place the Brihadratha dynasty much earlier, in the legendary period. For a trivia card, -600 is the most likely answer.

-600

Melchizedek appears in Genesis 14 in the time of Abraham, and the Bible gives no death date for him. The best I can do is anchor him to Abraham's traditional dating. Abraham is usually placed around 2000-1800 BCE. A common approximation for the Genesis 14 encounter is about -1900, and a death date has to be a guess near that.

Some traditional chronologies instead put Abraham around 2000 BCE. Other traditions identify Melchizedek with Shem, who would have died around 2158 BCE by Ussher's chronology, but that identification is itself uncertain. I'll go with a guess near the Abraham-era estimate.

-1900

Aristotle's Poetics is usually dated to around 335 BCE, when he was teaching in Athens. It is a lecture text rather than a book published at a known date, so the year is an estimate.

-335

Ashurbanipal's death date is debated. The traditional date is c. 631 BCE, and some scholars prefer 627 BCE. Many sources give 631 BCE, so I'll use that.

-631

The Rashtrakuta dynasty is usually dated from Dantidurga's rise around 753 CE, when he overthrew the Chalukyas of Badami. Earlier Rashtrakuta lineages existed, but 753 is the standard founding date for the imperial dynasty.

753

The question is ambiguous. Ozone depletion as a phenomenon began being observed in the late 1970s, with the Antarctic ozone hole discovered in 1985. Molina and Rowland's CFC hypothesis was published in 1974. Measurable depletion began around 1970s. A trivia card on "year started" probably expects a single year, so I'll go with the 1970s start, picking 1970.

1970

The Utah monolith was discovered on November 18, 2020, and was removed on the night of November 27, 2020. So the year it ended is 2020.

2020

ABC was formed in 1943 when NBC's Blue Network was sold and became independent, and it was renamed the American Broadcasting Company in 1943. The Blue Network was originally founded in 1927, and ABC itself was officially established in 1943, so the answer is 1943.

1943

Karnak's construction began in the Middle Kingdom, around 2000 BCE under Senusret I (c. 1971–1926 BCE). The earliest known structures date to about 1970 BCE, so I'll use -1970.

-1970

Samuel's traditional dating places his birth around 1100 BCE, though estimates vary. Ussher's chronology gives 1171 BCE, while many modern estimates place him around 1100–1070 BCE. I'll go with about 1100 BCE.

-1100

Gaius Cassius Longinus, the assassin of Julius Caesar, is usually dated to about 86 BCE, though the exact year is uncertain. He died at Philippi in 42 BCE. Sources generally give his birth as 86 BCE, and some give 85.

-86

Judah, the fourth son of Jacob, has no securely attested birth date. Traditional biblical chronology places Jacob around 1900-1800 BCE, which would put Judah's birth roughly in the 18th or 19th century BCE. A Ussher-style calculation gives about 1752 BCE for Judah, and the Jewish traditional (Seder Olam) date is around 1565 BCE by Anno Mundi reckoning, though I'm less sure of that figure. I'll go with the Ussher-style estimate.

-1752

Diogenes of Sinope is traditionally said to have been born around 412 BCE, though some accounts place it around 404 BCE. The commonly cited date is c. 412 BCE.

-412
